research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 11850 (signed 1975-04-08; 40 FR 16187; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11850.txt, read in full) renounces first use in war of chemical herbicides and, except in defensive military modes to save lives, of riot control agents, and directs the Secretary of Defense to prohibit their use without advance Presidential approval and to prescribe implementing rules. Identity: the heading of Executive Order 11850 on the renunciation of certain uses in war of chemical herbicides and riot control agents at 40 FR 16187, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory held only the four example paragraphs (a) to (d) and the run after them, so I replaced it with eight clauses (inventory override): the statement of policy, paragraphs (a), (b), (c) and (d), the recital and sections 1 and 2. Own terms: no clause has an end date or ending condition; section 2 directs rules to be prescribed without a date and the held evidence does not show whether they were, so no performance end is claimed. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 11850 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy, the 1989 codification snapshot and the notes to 50 U.S.C. 1512 (matches of 11850 as a page or docket number are unrelated); the dossier chain has no event and lists no actor. The held note to 50 U.S.C. 1512 restates the order's policy in statute (Public Law 109-163, section 1232) and refers in its report provision to the continuing validity of the order, which supports its continuation and ends nothing. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 2, 2 and 0 hits for the order number respectively. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate rests on the held original text and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); the 2006 statute text is corroboration and not a packet source, and the rules prescribed under section 2 are not held.
